target: stdout carries exactly one envelope and nothing else — sourcing .env executes whatever is in it, so a stray echo lands ahead of the envelope and every caller that pipes to jq gets garbage
cmd: printf 'OPENROUTER_API_KEY=k\necho POLLUTED\n' > .env; printf '%s' '{"objective":"x"}' | MOCK_RESPONSE_FILE="$FIXTURES/sol-transport/openrouter-with-cost.json" bash "$PLUGIN_ROOT/scripts/call_sol.sh" --mode adversary --via openrouter 2>/dev/null > out.txt; if jq -e . out.txt >/dev/null 2>&1 && [ "$(jq -s length out.txt)" = 1 ]; then echo CLEAN_ENVELOPE; else echo CONTRACT_BROKEN; fi
